title: Few facts, matched to the exact topic
statement: Fetch an item's sources and facts by its exact topic or objective, not its unit, and give the writer only the few that match, since other topics' facts blend in.
example: The research summary advises the 10-15 most relevant facts rather than all 3,347.
detail: With facts drawn for the whole unit, the AP question work expected an item on one topic to mix in another topic's facts, or to get no help from them (`icloud-work/ML learnings/knowledge_and_rag_pipeline.md`). Facts were then matched to the item's topic cluster first, which was reported as improving relevance, with no pass-rate figure (`icloud-work/ML learnings/week_of_apr_21.md`). The research summary adds the Lost-in-the-Middle problem, that facts in the middle of a long block are ignored most, and advises giving the 10-15 most relevant facts rather than all 3,347 (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_rag_factual_grounding.md`).
against: The cluster change's effect was never measured: "Cluster-matched facts > unit-level-only improved relevance." (`icloud-work/ML learnings/infrastructure_and_tooling.md`, line 158). The writer was only ever given five facts (`icloud-work/ML learnings/knowledge_and_rag_pipeline.md`, line 208), so the comparison with all 3,347 answers a setup nobody ran. Another note favours more facts in the store, not the prompt: "More facts = better coverage = fewer hallucination opportunities." (`icloud-work/ML learnings/knowledge_and_rag_pipeline.md`, line 228). The 75% rests on 8 items, and the two rates come from runs of different sizes, so the size of the gain is uncertain (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/data/model_findings.md`).

evidence.quote: If the question topic was about Progressivism but the injected facts were about immigration, the model might generate a question that mixed both — or the curriculum facts wouldn't help at all.
**Impact:** Cluster-matched facts are more relevant to the specific question being generated. The model has better grounding for the specific topic rather than unit-level context.

**More context injection / longer fact lists:** The Lost-in-the-Middle problem means that making the fact list longer reduces the model's ability to use it. Better to use a retriever (Technique 7) to inject only the 10-15 most relevant facts rather than all 3,347.
- **Context position**: Facts buried in the middle of a long context block are more likely to be ignored than facts at the very beginning or end (Lost-in-the-Middle problem).
Cluster-matched facts (not just unit-level) improved relevance.

1. **Topic mismatch is the root failure cause.** Bank indexed by (course, unit) — 50 entries spanning 30+ years and multiple topics. A "Failure of Reconstruction" request had only 2/50 chance of getting Reconstruction documents.
We were doing fuzzy topic-based MongoDB search and sometimes getting irrelevant facts.
